newsitem.title: UK: British Aerospace slips after Boeing merger.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace slips after Boeing merger.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace slipped in early trade on Monday as analysts said the merger between two U.S. competitors announced on Sunday would be negative for the group in the short term.
By 0907 GMT the stock was down 12 pence at 1113-1/2p.

Analysts said the deal between rivals Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas would allow the merged group to compete aggressively, not only in third markets such as the middle and far east, but also in key European markets.
"This is what the Europeans have really got to watch out for," said BZW analyst Nick Cunningham.

Boeing and McDonnell Douglas said at the weekend they planned a $13.3 billion merger which would give them a combined 75 percent of the commercial aircraft market, dwarfing European aircraft consortium Airbus's 20 percent share.

Airbus -- currently in talks to become an integrated company rather than a partnership -- is made up of Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
